note: Dated observation log. Every row is one live fetch, with the URL requested, what came back, and the session/shuffle tokens the response carried. Two caveats are recorded rather than smoothed over. (1) The second pass for SUB-04 and SUB-05 returned the SAME Amazon session id and the same btn_ref as the first pass, so the two passes share a session context and are weaker evidence than two independent sessions would be - see flag IF-06. (2) Session ids and btn_ref values are per-request tracking tokens; they are recorded because they are part of what was observed, and because a previous session found the btn_ref differs across days (ledger flag F-21).
method: Each URL was requested once per pass and the resolved URL and page title read from the response.

rows.why_it_matters: An unissued 9-character code of the same shape as the submitted codes is answered with a 404 rather than a product page. The five supplied codes therefore resolve because they are issued lookups, not because the service ignores its input and falls back to something arbitrary. It does not follow that the destination is the product the owner intended.
